newsitem.title: UK: Utd Utilities to hold board meeting on Tues.
newsitem.headline: Utd Utilities to hold board meeting on Tues.

text.p: Britain's United Utilities confirmed on Monday that it would be holding a special board meeting on Tuesday to discuss the future of the company's management.

A company spokesman told Reuters that the main agenda of the meeting, reported in weekend newspapers, will be a discussion on the views canvassed by Peter Middleton, a non-executive director of the company.

Middleton, who is also the chairman of Barclays investment banking unit, has been canvassing opinion among United's institutional investors on the role of its chairman Desmond Pitcher. Some investors have called for Pitcher to step down.
"The meeting will discuss the views canvassed by Peter Middleton...it is the main item," the spokesman said.
"It's a meeting with institutional investors on the future of the company's management," he said.
Pitcher's surprise sacking of chief executive Brian Staples last month fuelled concerns about a board split and prompted some investors to demand that he step down.

Some institutional investors are also believed to be keen on seeing Pitcher taking up a non-executive role in the company. Newspaper reports over the weekend said Pitcher, once considered the highest-paid of all the heads of privatised utilities, has been fighting to persuade boardroom colleagues to support him on Tuesday and present a united front of shareholders.
Investors, however, ignored the possible boardroom squabbles on Monday as its share price rose 6 1/2 pence to 707 1/2 at 0900 GMT.
